doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Playing in Europe versus America
summary: Europeans appreciate jazz more because they hear less of it.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That’s marvelous insights. You toured Europe I think in 1974.
Well I’ve been to Europe a lot of times, you know, almost every year I go there with somebody it seems like, yeah.
How is that different from playing in the United States?

You mean playing in Europe compared to this country? Well you know, what you’ve got to realize that you know Europe, people don’t hear jazz to the degree that they do in this country. They don’t have the exposure that we do in America. I mean there’s a lot of jazz played over there but not like here. So naturally they appreciate it more. Yeah. I think that’s one of the reasons they do. Everybody says well people, a lot of musicians over the years, oh Europe, yeah, yeah. And some of them go over there and live over there. But sometimes when they live over there then it’s a little different story, then they’re local. And they’re not heroes quite to the extent they were before.
